summary: The design addresses real portability gaps, but its highest risks are configuration trust boundaries, arbitrary host execution, and duplicating existing runner/lint abstractions. The implementation should preserve the current adapter and test-command contracts while making primary-checkout reads, mixed-repository scoping, and setup outcomes explicit.

suggestions.title: Separate primary-checkout configuration from worktree configuration
suggestions.rationale: `resolve_sandbox_mode` currently reads the linked worktree’s `pyproject.toml`, while `load_launch_config` deliberately reads the primary checkout because the worktree is writable by the sandbox. The new reader must make this distinction explicit; otherwise a sandboxed branch can alter the mode, runner setup, or host command used later. Add an explicit primary-root loader or require the caller to pass the primary root, and test tampered worktree config independently from runner settings consumed inside that worktree.

suggestions.title: Version and strongly type the new config blocks
suggestions.rationale: `SddConfig` uses `extra="forbid"`, so adding runner/toolchain fields creates hard version skew. The runner registry currently converts arbitrary scalar TOML values into strings, which is too weak for validating cwd containment, commands, suffixes, timeouts, and overrides. Add an explicit config schema version and typed nested models, with a documented migration or minimum-version error before installers emit new fields.

suggestions.title: Represent host setup as argv rather than an implicit shell string
suggestions.rationale: The proposed setup command executes outside the sandbox, but the current config already stores free-form shell text for `test_command`. Native artifact builds provide a safer existing precedent: list-based argv, explicit cwd, bounded timeout, captured output, and a Python placeholder. Make setup use the same model, or require an explicit shell mode with clear warning and validation; reject cwd escapes and avoid interpolating repository-controlled text into a shell.

suggestions.title: Define setup state and failure semantics separately from native sync
suggestions.rationale: `ensure_worktree` currently catches native-sync exceptions, emits warnings, and continues, while `NativeSyncReport` only describes artifact copying/building. The accepted setup rule says failures block, reruns depend on lockfile changes, and JSON must report the outcome. Add a distinct setup report and durable input hash covering the command, relevant lockfiles, and configuration; test first creation, reuse, lockfile change, command change, failure, and `--no-setup` so native-sync warnings cannot accidentally suppress a setup failure.

suggestions.title: Unify normal and verdict test execution paths
suggestions.rationale: `select_tests.py` already runs invocations in `worktree / invocation.cwd` in verdict mode, but its ordinary `--run` path uses `cwd=worktree`. The ordinary path also appends `--timeout` to every runner, whereas the option is pytest-specific. Extract one bounded executor used by both paths, preserving report paths relative to the selected cwd, and add Vitest and Cargo regression tests for cwd, timeout, missing binaries, and report generation.

suggestions.title: Make profiles feed the existing runner registry instead of creating a second execution model
suggestions.rationale: The repository already has `RunnerRegistry`, `RunnerAdapter`, launcher normalization, per-runner settings, tier validation, and adapters for pytest, Vitest, Cargo, and parrot-e2e. The detector should produce validated registry defaults/overrides, while adapters remain responsible for invocation and reports; otherwise profile commands and runner adapters will diverge on timeouts, reports, and eligibility.

suggestions.title: Resolve profiles per configured root, not once per repository
suggestions.rationale: The planner already treats runner settings and cwd as per-runner data, and Vitest mirrors source files relative to its configured cwd. A single root-level profile cannot safely classify a mixed repository such as ai-parrot with its Svelte UI. Resolve a profile for the repository root and each configured runner cwd, then map changed files to exactly one profile; require an explicit override for overlapping roots.

suggestions.title: Make the Vitest package manager part of the adapter invocation contract
suggestions.rationale: `VitestAdapter.binaries` and `invocation` hard-code pnpm, while launcher normalization already recognizes npm, yarn, and npx. Detecting a package manager without passing it into invocation leaves npm/yarn repositories unable to run scoped tests. Add a validated package-manager setting with deterministic precedence (`packageManager`, lockfile, explicit override), and test equivalent invocations for pnpm, npm, yarn, and unsupported managers.

suggestions.title: Extend the engine boundary beyond the Python-only lint implementation
suggestions.rationale: `run_lint_pass` exits early unless changed files end in `.py`, requires ruff, and its `LintConfig` only models black/ruff behavior. The merge engine invokes it for every task, then separately runs a ruff-only banned-import gate in `fidelity.py`. Supporting Node or Rust requires a profile operation contract covering suffix selection, bounded commands, autofix commit behavior, residual findings, and the Python-only fidelity gate; changing only `lint.py` will leave foreign tasks silently unvalidated or incorrectly gated.

suggestions.title: Turn the existing foreign-repository harness into the Node/Vitest acceptance fixture
suggestions.rationale: The repository already has a wheel-only foreign-repository harness that installs SDD assets, invokes every documented helper, checks no traceback behavior, and verifies guard behavior, but its fixture is only a README-based non-Python repository. Extend that fixture with package.json, lockfile, Vitest files, configured cwd, and a setup command; this gives deterministic coverage of install, config precedence, runner selection, guard rewriting, worktree setup, and `--run` without depending on an external navigator checkout.

suggestions.title: Make contract probing consume profile capabilities while retaining deterministic commands
suggestions.rationale: The shipped contract probe hard-codes Python-only absence checks (`--include=*.py`) and fixed shell commands. A language-aware probe should consume a small, profile-provided capability table for suffixes, symbol/outline, and absence checks, with safe fixed command templates; arbitrary configured project scripts would make a read-only fact checker non-reproducible and unsafe. Add explicit fallback behavior when a profile lacks symbol support.

suggestions.title: Expand asset parity checks to every changed host twin
suggestions.rationale: The repository’s parity test covers coder rules, while the foreign-repo tests validate installed behavior and the proposal requires synchronized Claude, Agent, Agents, and Codex assets. Prompt/template neutralization can therefore drift in a host-specific copy even when current tests pass. Add a parameterized check for every modified semantic asset and verify installed bytes against the packaged source in the existing asset-sync gate.
